correctness.rationale: Working in intrinsic m-dimensional H_m, Gaussian support of the centrally symmetric polytope equals H=max(R_m,a T_m), with R_m=max cyclic |Gi-Gi+1| and T_m=max_i |Gi-G0| for independent standard Gaussians. Orthogonal Gaussian radial factor Q~chi_m is independent of sphere direction; eta_m=E Q gives exact E H=eta_m E W/2. Radial fluctuations times O_p(sqrt(log m)) are o_p(1/sqrt(log m)). Gaussian extrema imply T_m=r_m+|G0|+o_p(1); disjoint edge lower bounds and union upper bounds give R_m=sqrt2 r_m+o_p(1). For a_m=sqrt2+c/r_m their max gives the positive-part half-normal crossover, mean by L1 Gaussian maximal bounds, and strict spoke-exposure limit with no tie at the continuous cutoff. For fixed a<sqrt2, standardized adjacent rim edge normals are 1-dependent with correlation -1/2, joint exceedance <=4exp(-2u²/3), so neighbor clusters vanish at u=b_2m+s_2m x and Poisson rare-event approximation yields the stated Gumbel law. For fixed a>sqrt2 spoke dominates and a|Z| remains. Independent support identity replay covered 640 Gaussian cases; slow finite-size exposure diagnostics were not used to infer the limit.
